chunks: Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah narrated from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام:
That he ruled: “A corrupt young boy should be placed under legal restriction until he becomes rational.”
And he عليه السلام ruled regarding debt: “Its holder is imprisoned; then, if his insolvency and need become clear, his way is released for him until he acquires wealth.”

And he عليه السلام ruled regarding a man who evades his creditors: “He is imprisoned, then action is ordered concerning him, so his wealth is divided among his creditors according to shares; if he refuses, it is sold and then divided among them.”

key_terms.الْمُفْسِدِ: one who acts corruptly or causes harm
key_terms.يُحْجَرَ: to be placed under legal restriction or interdiction

ai.seo_question: What did Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام rule about bankrupt debtors, evasive debtors, and legal restriction over minors?
ai.summary: This hadith records legal rulings from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning interdiction, insolvency, and creditors’ rights. It establishes restriction over a corrupt minor until sound reason appears, distinguishes between a genuinely insolvent debtor and one who evades payment, and affirms proportional distribution of assets among creditors.
